page: Microsoft Azure E8d_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EDv4 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores running at 2.6 GHz, utilizing hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 vector extensions. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 307 GB SSD, and virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results place the E8d_v4 in the average performance tier for most standard compute and memory tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests scored 1410.98 and 7432.24 respectively, while PassMark CPU and memory scores also landed in the middle 50% range. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is strong at 413.99 GB/sec, though large uncached read and write operations drop to a weaker bottom-25% tier at 28.37 GB/sec and 22.01 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average levels, with Redis handling 6.53 million operations per second. However, single-threaded compression, static web serving, and LLM inference tasks show weaker relative performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E8d_v4 offers a high-density memory profile and integrated local SSD storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for temporary data. The main tradeoff lies in its processing speed and memory bandwidth under heavy, uncached sequential workloads, which perform in the lower percentiles. It is not optimized for intensive LLM inference or high-throughput web serving.

This server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from local scratch space, such as relational databases, caching layers like Redis, data compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio without extreme compute demands.
